fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration, effective December 8, 2017 and recorded in Weld County on April 24, 2018, names Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District No. 1 as the body that enforces its covenants and provides design review.
quote: THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, RESTRICTIONS AND EASEMENTS FOR THE GOLDEN EAGLE ACRES SUBDIVISION (the "Declaration") are made and entered into to be effective as of the 8th day of December, 2017 … WHEREAS, the Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District No. 1 (the "Metropolitan District," as hereinafter more fully defined) was organized under the laws of the State of Colorado pursuant to the Service Plan for Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan Districts Nos. 1, 2 and 3 … which Metropolitan District shall, pursuant to Section 32-1-1004 (8) of the Colorado Revised Statutes, enforce the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, and provide design review services as set forth herein
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (recitals, p. 4)
notes: Scanned PDF (43 pages) with an OCR text layer; key pages checked against the page images on 2026-09-26. The recording stamp on every page reads reception 4393472, 04/24/2018. The body's section numbers in Article III run one ahead of the table of contents (the body has Section 3.14 Completion of Landscaping and 3.15 Grade and Drainage; the contents list them as 3.13 and 3.14); pages cite the body numbers.

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration says it does not create a common interest community and is not governed by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act.
quote: WHEREAS, this Declaration does not create a Common Interest Community, as defined by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act at C.R.S. §38-33.3-103(8), as amended; therefore, this Declaration and its Covenants shall not be governed by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act or any provisions thereof.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (recitals, p. 5)
notes: The state HOA turf rule (co-hoa-backyard-detached) sits in CCIOA; the special-district and restrictive-covenant rule (co-special-district-backyard) is C.R.S. 37-60-126(11)(a.5). Which one reaches a lot here is left to the district or counsel in copy.

fact: Nothing may be built, placed, altered, planted or installed on a Golden Eagle Acres lot without the Architectural Review Committee's written approval of complete plans, and the declaration's improvements include patios, sprinkler systems, play structures, retaining walls, exterior light fixtures, any change of grade or drainage pattern, and planting or material changes to landscaping, sod and gravel.
quote: No Improvements shall be constructed, erected, placed, altered, planted, applied or installed upon any Lot unless said Improvements are in full compliance with the provisions of the Project Documents and unless complete plans and specifications have been first submitted to and approved in writing by the ARC. … "Improvement(s)" shall mean and include the following: (a) the construction, installation, alteration, demolition in whole or in part, or expansion of any exterior improvement, building, structure, appurtenance, or other improvements, including, but not limited to, buildings, outbuildings, swimming pools, tennis courts, patios, patio covers, awnings, … sprinkler systems, garages, driveways, parking areas, fences, including gates in fences, basketball backboards and hoops, swing-sets or other play structures, screening walls, retaining walls, stairs, decks, exterior light fixtures … (b) the staking, clearing, grading, excavation, filling or similar disturbance to the surface of the land, including without limitation any change of grade, change of ground level, change of drainage pattern … (c) all initial planting of and subsequent material modifications to landscaping, hedges, windbreaks, berming, plantings, trees, shrubs, flowers, vegetables, sod, gravel, bark
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Sec. 2.3.1 and Sec. 1.1.16, pp. 7 and 9)

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration requires a landscaping plan done by a professional landscape designer or contractor, submitted with a review fee and compliance deposit and approved before landscaping starts, showing fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rock, timbers, the sprinkler system, nursery sizes and species and a drainage and grading plan.
quote: For any Lot an additional review fee and Compliance Deposit must be paid to the ARC with submission of a landscaping plan. Landscaping plans may be submitted with the Construction Drawings but must be submitted and approved PRIOR TO COMMENCEMENT OF LANDSCAPING. Plans must depict fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rock, timbers, sprinkler system, sizes and species of nursery materials, and include a drainage and grading plan that coincides with the builder's, and shows any Improvements or alterations thereto. Landscape plans must be done by a professional landscape designer/contractor.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Sec. 3.14.1 Landscaping Plans, p. 20)
notes: Checked against the page image of p. 20. The list names no artificial or synthetic turf.

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration has each owner landscape all of the lot not covered by a building, fence or other structure, up to the street curb, within 180 days after construction is completed between April 1 and October 1, or otherwise by the next October 1, on plans the ARC approves first.
quote: the Owner (other than the Declarant, or a builder with the express written approval of the Declarant) of each Lot shall install landscaping on all of the Lot which is not covered or enclosed by a building, fence or other structure, including all street trees and landscaping up to the street curb, and shall thereafter maintain such landscaping in a neat and attractive condition … shall install landscaping on such Lot within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days after the completion of construction of Improvements on such Lot by such Owner if said completion occurs between April 1 and October 1; if said completion does not occur between such dates, then such landscaping shall be installed by such Owner by the following October 1. … Landscaping plans and other required documents shall be in accordance with the Guidelines and shall be submitted to the ARC for review and approval prior to the installation of landscaping
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Sec. 3.14 Completion of Landscaping, p. 20)

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration has each owner keep the lot's grading at the slope and pitch set by final grading and send any change to the established drainage to the ARC as a plan.
quote: Each Owner shall maintain the grading upon his Lot (including grading around the building foundation) at the slope and pitch fixed by the final grading thereof, including landscaping and maintenance of the slopes, so as to maintain the established drainage. Each Owner agrees that he will not in any way interfere with the established drainage pattern over his Lot. In the event that it is necessary or desirable to change the established drainage over any Lot, then the Owner thereof shall submit a plan to the ARC for its review and approval
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Sec. 3.15.1, pp. 20-21)

fact: Golden Eagle Acres' Architectural Control Handbook, effective April 16, 2020, requires a $50 Landscape Review Fee and ARC approval before landscaping starts, on plans showing fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rocks, railroad ties, the sprinkler system, nursery sizes and species and a drainage and grading plan, and bars changes to the approved drainage or grading plans.
quote: EFFECTIVE AS OF APRIL 16, 2020 … Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines … A Landscape Review Fee in the amount of $50, made payable to Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District is required with the submission of landscaping plans. ARC approval must be obtained by the applicant prior to commencement of landscaping. Plans must depict fences, decks, sod, seeded areas, retaining walls, rocks, railroad ties, sprinkler system, sizes and species of nursery materials, and include a drainage and grading plan that coincides with the builders. Builders and homeowners will not alter the city approved drainage or grading plans.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), cover and Landscaping Guidelines & Submittal Instructions
notes: Text-based PDF (17 pages, file dated March 26, 2025), read in full 2026-09-26. The district's Architectural Review page links it as 'Design Guidelines'.

fact: Neither the Golden Eagle Acres handbook nor its recorded declaration mentions artificial turf or putting greens; the handbook permits xeriscaping case by case, in accordance with Colorado law, on professionally designed plans.
quote: Xeriscaping will be permitted on a case-by-case basis in accordance with Colorado law. Plans must be professionally designed, incorporating different materials (i.e. mulch, breeze, river rock, cobble, etc), edging, trees, and plants into the plan.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Landscaping
notes: Searched the full handbook text, the declaration's OCR text (landscaping pages checked against the page images), the water rules, the ARC application and the service plan on 2026-09-26 for turf, synthetic, artificial, nonvegetative and putting: no hits (the declaration's one 'golf' is 'golf carts' in its parking section).

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres handbook lays out every lot in three zones: Zone 1 around the home with trees, shrubs, flower beds and irrigated grass, its irrigated sod not to exceed 10,000 square feet so the lot stays inside its water allotment, and a front yard of sod, 3 trees of at least 2-inch caliper, five 5-gallon shrubs and ten 1-gallon perennials; Zone 2 of irrigated native grasses, plants and trees at the sides and rear; and Zone 3 at the back in drought-tolerant fescue or native prairie grass.
quote: Landscaping designs will have three zones and shall be in accordance in general with the attached Landscape Plans and illustrated typical lot layout. All landscaping plans must be approved by the ARC. In general, Zone #1 will be surrounding the home and feature trees, shrubs, flower beds and irrigated grass. Irrigated sod should not exceed more that 10,000 sq. ft. to ensure maximum water allotment is not exceeded. Front yard landscaping shall be made up of sod, 3 trees of at least 2-inch caliper, five 5-gallon shrubs or bushes and ten 1-gallon perennials as illustrated in the typical lot layout. Zone #2 is generally located at the sides and rear of the lot and connects Zone #1 to the neighboring lots. Zone #2. The plantings will be a mix of irrigated native grasses, plants and trees. Zone #3 will be located in the back of the lots and be either a drought tolerant fescue or a native prairie grass and may also include trees and planting. Deciduous street trees must be planted 3 feet from the back edge of the curb every forty feet in addition to the 3 trees located in the front yard
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Landscaping
notes: 'more that' is the handbook's own typo. The attached Landscape Plans and typical lot layout the handbook refers to are not in the posted PDF.

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres handbook, which follows the declaration in barring open fires, allows gas or wood fire pits once detailed drawings of them on the landscape plan are approved.
quote: Per the Declaration of Covenants, no open fires are permitted. Fires on the property must be fully contained within the fireplace. Gas or wood fire pits are allowed. Detailed drawings of said fire pits must be shown on the landscape plan and receive approval from the ARB before they can be installed.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Fireplaces
notes: 'ARB' is the handbook's wording for the ARC in this one bullet.

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres handbook wants exterior lighting subdued and residential, with concealed area-light sources in all white or all pale yellow, no excessive glare or bright continuous yard lighting, and the lighting design approved by the ARC.
quote: Exterior lighting shall be subdued, understated, and residential in nature. Area lighting shall be concealed light sources and shall be either all white or all pale yellow. In all cases excessive glare to the neighboring properties or bright continuous yard lighting shall be avoided. The approval of the exterior lighting design must be approved by the ARC.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Lighting

fact: Every Golden Eagle Acres home must have a back patio or deck of at least 120 square feet, and homes sit 40 feet from the front line (30 with a side-load or recessed garage), 20 feet from the sides and 50 feet from the back line.
quote: Every home shall include a back patio/deck that is a minimum of one hundred twenty (120) square feet. … Front property line setbacks shall be 40 feet for homes that have a protruding garage. … Front property line setbacks shall be 30 feet for homes that have side load or recessed garages. … Side property line setbacks shall be 20 feet for all homes. … Back property line setbacks shall be 50 feet for all homes.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Porches and Balconies; Setbacks

fact: Golden Eagle Acres fencing needs ARC approval: perimeter fences are 48-inch three-rail cedar, with black metal mesh allowed on the inside, and solid 6-foot cedar screening may stand only on or within the building envelope.
quote: ARC approval is required for all fencing additions or modifications. All perimeter lot line fencing shall be 48” high, three-rail cedar wood fencing. Perimeter lot line fencing is not required except on the rear lot lines of Lots 1-30 and Lots 34-39 and the northern side yards of Lots 1 and 34. … Black metal mesh-type material is permitted to be installed on the inside of the fence. … Interior fencing shall be solid cedar fencing and installed on or within the building envelope. Solid fencing must be 6-feet high and shall be built using 1” X 6” dog-eared style fence.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Fencing

fact: Under the Golden Eagle Acres declaration a dog run may not be visible from a street or from the ground level of any lot, must sit at least 5 feet from any property line and must be screened so the dog is not visible from neighboring lots.
quote: No clotheslines, drying yards, service yards, wood piles, storage areas or chain-linked (or other) dog runs, shall be so located as to be visible from a street or from the ground level of any Lot. Dog runs shall not be located within five (5) feet from any property line, and shall be screened by approved materials so that the dog therein is not visible from neighboring Lots. "Invisible" electric fences shall generally be permitted along property lines.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Sec. 3.5.2 Dog Runs, etc., p. 15)

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres district's website says ARC applications go in through the homeowner portal with a $50 review fee, the ARC responds within 30 days of a complete submission, and approved work must be finished within 1 year.
quote: Improvements or alterations on Lots within Golden Eagle Acres Metro Districts are subject to review by the Architectural Review Committee (ARC). … There is a $50 Review Fee, which can be paid online through the portal or by check. The ARC will respond to your application within 30 days following complete submission. Approved improvements or alternations must be completed within 1 year following ARC approval. Please submit your application in the homeowner portal.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Architectural Review page

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration gives the ARC 45 calendar days after a complete submission, treats a request not approved by then as disapproved, lets an owner appeal an adverse ARC decision to the district board within 10 calendar days, and makes the compliance deposit non-refundable if approved work is not completed within one year.
quote: The ARC shall approve or disapprove all requests for approval within forty-five (45) calendar days after the complete submission of all plans, specifications, and other materials and information which the ARC may require in conjunction therewith. … Failure to approve within forty-five (45) calendar days shall be deemed disapproval. … In the event the ARC decides a request for architectural approval that is adverse to the applicant, then the applicant shall have the right to an appeal of such decision to the full Governing Board, upon a written request therefor submitted to the Governing Board within ten (10) calendar days after such decision by the ARC. … Failure to complete the proposed Improvement within one (1) year after the date of approval of the application or to complete the Improvement in complete conformance with the conditions and requirements of the approval shall constitute noncompliance and the Compliance Deposit shall become non-refundable
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Secs. 2.5, 2.6 and 2.7, p. 11)

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres handbook has the district manager oversee ARC review and route every application and fee, warns in its construction section that reviews may take 15 to 45 days, and charges $50 for each additional submittal.
quote: The ARC has appointed … District Manager, to oversee the ARC review process. All applications, fees, and submittal forms shall be sent through their office … ARC reviews may take between 15-45 days to complete. Please plan accordingly. … There will be an additional $50 charged for additional submittals to the ARC. For example, color charts or samples, plans for additions or exterior changes- or anything else missing from the original submittal.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Architectural Review Committee and Construction Guidelines & Submittal Instructions
notes: The elided name is the district manager's firm; it is left out of the rendered quote because its first word matches a Denver-metro town name the site never prints. The district's District Management page names the same firm and manager.

fact: Golden Eagle Acres' ARC application, sent with a $50 fee, lists front and rear landscaping as separate requests and has the owner agree to get required building permits, call Colorado 811 for locates, leave drainage patterns alone without written approval, and resubmit any change from the approved plan.
quote: A $50 Review Fee is required with all application submittals. … ☐ Front Landscaping … ☐ Rear Landscaping … ☐ Patio Cover / Awning / Pergola … ARC approval does not constitute approval of the local building or zoning department, drainage design, structural or engineering safety and/or soundness. … I understand that it is my responsibility and obligation to obtain all required building permits, to contact Colorado 811 for utility locates … I further agree not to alter existing drainage patterns on the Lot without the express approval in writing by the Board or ARC. … Any variation from the original application must be resubmitted for approval.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres ARC Submittal Form, Application for Modifications or Improvements (PDF dated December 11, 2025)

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres declaration requires owners to irrigate from the district's non-potable system under its water rules, calls that water unfit for people to drink, and has owners keep animals from drinking it or from harmful exposure to it.
quote: Property Owners living within the Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision or any of the Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan Districts shall be required to utilize the Golden Eagle Acres Non-Potable Water System and abide by the Districts' Water Rules and Regulations … Non-potable irrigation water is not fit for human consumption. … To the extent such water may be harmful to animals, the Owner or keeper of such animals shall take appropriate precautions to prevent the animal from drinking the non-potable irrigation water or otherwise exposing the animal to such water in a manner which would be damaging to the animal's health.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, and Easements for Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision and Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Weld County Reception 4393472, recorded 04/24/2018 (Secs. 7.2 and 7.3, p. 31)

fact: Golden Eagle Acres' water rules supply non-potable water only for irrigating landscaping, allow sprinklers from 7 pm to 9 am and drip from 6 pm to 11 am, give even addresses Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday and odd addresses Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, and have the board cut watering from 3 days a week to 2 in a drought or shortage.
quote: It is currently contemplated that irrigation water under this Article IV is being provided by the Districts for the sole use of irrigating landscaping of all irrigable areas within the Golden Eagle Acres Subdivision. … Irrigation sprinklers should only be operated between the hours of 7 pm and 9 am. Drip irrigation systems may be operated between the hours of 6 pm and 11 am. … Even Numbered Single Family Addresses: Watering permitted three (3) days per week on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays only … Odd Numbered Single Family Addresses: Watering permitted three (3) days per week on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays only … During periods of drought or shortage, the board of directors for the Districts shall reduce delivery of non-potable irrigation water from 3 days to 2 days per week.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Amended and Restated Water Rules and Regulations (effective March 4, 2021), Art. IV and Secs. 4.4.1-4.4.3
notes: The district's Non-Potable Watering Schedule & Service Rates page (https://www.goldeneagleacres.com/non-potable-watering-schedule-service-rates) posts the same hours, days and rates, read 2026-09-26.

fact: Each Golden Eagle Acres lot is allocated 228,000 gallons of irrigation water a year, billed at $20.00 a month during the irrigation season plus $3.43 per 1,000 gallons, rising to $9.43 per 1,000 gallons past the allotment, in a season that runs about May 1 through October 31.
quote: Base Rate: $20.00 per month, per single family residential lot during the irrigation season. The irrigation season is approximately May 1st of each year through October 31st (weather depending). Plus: $3.43 per 1,000 gallons for usage billed monthly. Plus: If yearly usage exceeds 228,000 gallons a surcharge of an additional $6.00 per 1000 gallons shall apply. Thus $9.43 per 1,000 gallons for usage over 228,000 gallons in addition to any pro-rata share of necessary additional water costs. Each lot is allocated a total of 228,000 gallons annually.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Amended and Restated Water Rules and Regulations (effective March 4, 2021), Appendix A-1, Single Family Primary Irrigation Water Service Rates

fact: In a shortage Golden Eagle Acres' water rules limit deliveries to what the district's four Larimer and Weld Irrigation Company shares and four Larimer and Weld Reservoir Company shares can irrigate; the native and prairie grass on the 2 agricultural lots and 11 outlots gets only irrigation-company water, mostly in May and June, and is cut off first in a drought.
quote: In the event it appears that the unrestricted water use may endanger the adequacy of supply, the Districts shall reduce the delivery of non-potable water to only that which can be irrigated with the supply available from the water rights represented by the four (4) shares of the capital stock of the Larimer and Weld Irrigation Company and the four (4) shares of the capital stock of the Larimer and Weld Reservoir Company owned by the Districts. … The prairie, pasture and native grasses grown on the 2 Agricultural Lots and 11 Outlots will be irrigated only with the water delivered by the Larimer and Weld Irrigation Company, which is available primarily during the months of May and June. The residential lots will be irrigated by water from the Larimer and Weld Irrigation Company when it is available early in the season with a shift to water made available by the Larimer and Weld Reservoir Company later in the season. … During periods of drought when a sufficient supply of irrigation water is not available, the Districts shall terminate the delivery of non-potable irrigation water to the Agricultural Lots and to the Outlots and, as necessary, limit the supply available to the remaining residential lots.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Amended and Restated Water Rules and Regulations (effective March 4, 2021), Sec. 4.4

fact: The Town of Severance lists Golden Eagle Acres among the subdivisions served by North Weld County Water District and among those on septic systems.
quote: NWCWD - North Weld County Water District for the subdivisions of Belmont Farms, Bridal Hill/Saddler Ridge, Casa Loma, Golden Eagle Acres, Hidden Valley Farm, and Soaring Eagle Ranch. … Septic - the subdivisions of Belmont Farms, Casa Loma, Golden Eagle Acres, Settler's Landing, and Soaring Eagle Ranch are on septic systems.
source_label: Town of Severance, Utility Services by Other Agencies

fact: The Golden Eagle Acres district describes a rural, large-lot neighborhood on the eastern edge of Severance whose 61 interior lots range from 1.25 to 2.5 acres, with a pedestrian sidewalk along the interior street and a small neighborhood pavilion.
quote: Golden Eagle Acres is a rural residential large lot neighborhood located on the eastern edge of Severance. … 61 interior lots range from 1.25 to 2.5 acres which allows the yard setbacks to be greatly increased and establish a diverse, gracious, open and attractive streetscape. There will be a 6' pedestrian sidewalk along the interior street through out the entire length of the community which ties to a small neighborhood pavilion area that provides a great opportunity for residents to connect within the neighborhood.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Community Plan page

fact: Weld County's parcel-lot map draws Golden Eagle Acres as 63 numbered lots and 11 outlots, with Lots 1 through 61 at about 1.05 to 2.42 acres (median about 1.26) and Lots 62 and 63 at about 15.6 and 9.0 acres.
quote: SUBCODE: 7039 · SUBNAME: GOLDEN EAGLE ACRES · COMMONNAME: GOLDEN EAGLE ACRES (Subdivisions layer) … Parcel_Lots_open_data where SUBCODE = 7039: LOT 1 … 63; TRACT OUTLOT A … OUTLOT K
source_label: Weld County GIS, Parcel_Lots_open_data layer, subdivision code 7039 (Golden Eagle Acres), lot areas computed from the lot polygons, queried September 26, 2026
notes: Queried 2026-09-26 with where=SUBCODE=7039, outSR 2231 (Colorado North, US feet); shoelace area of each polygon. 74 polygons: 63 numbered lots (lot 4 is labelled '54474' in the data; its polygon sits between lots 3 and 5) and 11 outlots (A-K; F is labelled 'LOTLOT F' and H sits in the LOT field). Lots 1-61: min 1.053 acres (lot 57), median 1.261, max 2.416 (lot 33); lots 30, 31 and 33 are over 2 acres. Lot 62 about 15.57 acres, lot 63 about 9.05. fact: The Golden Eagle Acres handbook gives Lots 62 and 63 their own livestock management plan, with outbuildings up to 3,000 square feet set back at least 50 feet from every property line and one large animal per 3 acres.
quote: Livestock Management Plan, Additional Site Design Guidelines and Requirements for Lots 62 and 63 … The large outbuildings may be increased to be a maximum of 3,000 square feet. The small outbuildings may be increased up to 600 square feet. All outbuildings will have a 50' minimum setback from any property line. … No more than one large animal per every 3 acres will be allowed.
source_label: Golden Eagle Acres Architectural Control Handbook with Design Guidelines (effective April 16, 2020), Livestock Management Plan for Lots 62 and 63

fact: The service plan the Town of Severance approved for the Golden Eagle Acres metropolitan districts on August 21, 2017 covers about 158.173 acres and up to approximately 63 homes.
quote: Approved: August 21, 2017 … The area of the Initial District Boundaries includes approximately 158.173 acres. … The Project area consists of approximately 158.173 acres of land. … residing in up to approximately 63 units.
source_label: Service Plan for Golden Eagle Acres Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3, Town of Severance (approved August 21, 2017)
